This review is mine, left of my own volition.

review_samples.title: A great gift for children
review_samples.text: I was invited to read the award-winning Live Big series created for children by Kat Kronenberg and NetGalley in exchange for an honest review. Think Big is the last book in the trilogy. It seems to be written for older children, as it has sections that small children could not do. There are activities such as writing who they are, their gifts, goals, and passions; creating a family tree, and learning to be generous with not only those on the tree, but with community regarding safety, food and water, medicine. They are then to consider how blessed we all are, no matter our circumstances. This, too would be a wonderful book for slightly older children. What made The Grumpy Book Reviewer grumpy? Not a thing!

review_samples.title: Some good and some weird
review_samples.text: This is a fable involving African animals learning how to become their best selves. And by doing so, whether it's gathering food or saving others from a fire, they evolve into the creatures that we know today. And they share ways of being a great person (or animal in this case). The pictures are lively and colorful, which is attractive to the reader. But I had a really hard time with the giraffe, because in the beginning, he has no neck. I understand the story, that he evolves to growing the long neck to be helpful in getting food for the other animals, but that picture really bugged me for some reason. I know that the kudu also ends up changing its appearance, but honestly was not as familiar with that animal before this book. I think children are also going to question what is wrong with the giraffe's neck, because it reminds me more of a cow or something, instead. I did like how the author included factual tidbits about each of the animals, such as the dance that bees use to communicate with each other about where to find flowers. At the end of the book are several activities that children can do to re-engage them with the book as they go on hunts or interpret some of the information differently. Plus they can practice ways of living to the best of their abilities, using the Think Big ideas. Thank you to the publisher for fulfilling my review request via NetGalley. All thoughts and opinions are my own.

I highly recommend!

review_samples.title: This author deserves the support!
review_samples.text: I don't review too much on Amazon, but this author deserves the support! He has great talent there, and that's not very common these days unfortunately. His works remind me a bit of the early Stephen King novels. You can immediately feel that when somebody is a very promising author and also has a promising future ahead. This is what was already clear in the case of King in his early years. And this is also the case with A. R. Wise. I'm sure he has a promising future as a writer, or at least I hope so. Nowadays it's not easy to become famous, but some people would really deserve it! I like that Wise spends time to put everything necessary into his books: - suspense (most horror, thriller and crime books nowadays are plane boring. They try to be suspenseful, but they fail). Wise knows how to write suspense! - believable characters (his characters act like real people. The good ones are lovable, the bad ones aren't. That's a pretty basic thing, but I don't find this basic value in most books written these days, so this is why I'm mentioning it!) - heart-stirring and touching scenes: Even if he's not a huge drama fan and writer... (well as far I know he mostly writes horror) he's still very good at writing heart warming and nice scenes with real human feelings, emotions and relationships. - fear! (Have you every read a bad horror book that wasn't even scary at all? Well I had the unluck to read about a hundred of those. But this Deadlocked series are really as scary as a horror book should be!) In this episode I really liked the scene when the protagonist meets his mother. It was truly beautiful.

review_samples.title: Excellent
review_samples.text: I was completely unaware of Mo Hayder and her mystery novels until came across this soon to be posthumously published novel. While the premise of The Book of Sand seems to be the standard fare for sci-fi and fantasy (what attracted me to the book in the first place), the book is far more than what it seems at first glance. It weaves the stories of a desert quest occurring in harsh and brutal conditions, along with the search by a teen in Virginia who believes there’s more to her identity than she’s been told, into a complex tale that is more than your standard fantasy fare. For me, this was a page turner that was totally original in concept. Well written with strong lead characters. I can only hope that the reported future second volume will answer the questions raised by this impressive book. I received a copy of the book and I’m submitting this review voluntarily.

review_samples.title: It all sounds like a really good plot but sadly
review_samples.text: In the desert with deserted cities similar to those on Earth, there's a family trying to survive as they search for the way out before one of the other families finds it. In Virginia McKenzie is obsessed with sand, with the desert, with a sand-lizard only she can see until another person claims he can see it too. Why does the sand fascinate McKenzie so much and what is her connection to the family in the desert, who are hunted by the Djinni during the 'gray' nights? It all sounds like a really good plot but sadly the story itself jumps around. One paragraph is about the family and two paragraphs later it's McKenzie. There's not a lot of separation between the two 'worlds' in the chapters. There are some vivid details but not really enough to make the desert or McKenzie's life seem real, and I couldn't connect with any of the characters because of the jumping from here to there. There was no time to get to know the characters, especially the family. Only two really stand out, and one is a camel. I couldn't tell you much about the rest of the family because their descriptions and roles were vague. Designated chapters for each 'world' would've made the story move along better, allowing the reader to learn about the characters instead of dreading the next jump in the story. Designated chapters would've given the book another star. 2 Stars

review_samples.title: Prose-poem of middle-aged desire, unrequited
review_samples.text: Next to "Pomes Penyeach," this ranks rather low on my shelf compared to the major Joycean texts; it was published only in 1968. Still, it's around 3.5 stars, as it's a minor effort by a major genius. Richard Ellmann in his introduction to this edition accurately finds in its versifying unfortunate traces of the "anemic" style of his other verse. I agree. I doubt if ever it was offered anonymously to a press it would have seen the light of day, yet this is a value judgment impossible to realistically consider nearly a century later. Joyce sent it to "The Egoist" in 1914, but then withdrew it and instead, as Ellmann notes, pillaged it for use in his greater works in their slow progress. We come to these few lines knowing Joyce. So, we approach this as a prose-poem deserving respect and acclaim. It glows with the aura of its creator, as even a lesser work by a classic artist can dazzle intermittently. Most critics, following up clues that Ellmann in 1968 had not identified, match the dark Jewish girl that the narrator falls for, if only in his thoughts, with Amalia Popper, a student that Jim/Jamesy as named here becomes enchanted-- and possibly repulsed-- with as he teaches her in a Trieste classroom. The prose-poem floats into the realms of an older consciousness than Dedalus and a younger one than Bloom, but as Ellmann observes it prepares the way for "Ulysses" in its plunge into a stream of associations around the allure and horror of the feminine body. Written around the time Joyce turned thirty, the editor notes that even for late-blooming Italians, the time of adolescence generously granted ended, and "youth" began with the start of one's fourth decade. "A love poem which is never recited, it is Joyce's attempt at the sentimental education of a dark lady, a farewell to a phase of his life, and at the same time a discovery of a new form of imaginative expression." (ix) This wandering set of short reflections, evanescent and graphic, evocative and shadowed, shimmers like dreams half-recalled and half-articulated in words rather than a vanishing miasma of images, terrors, and langours. P.S. A collection of essays, "Giacomo Joyce: Envoys of the Other," has been published June 2007; it is astonishing that 400 pp. can emerge from scholarly attention to these eight large sheets of a few hundred lines at most, but such is the appeal of Joyce and the fervor of academics as they combine to make even this, one of his most evanescent and fragile texts, worthy of sustained scrutiny.

title: The River
features: In rural Missouri, Crawford County has had more than its share of wildlife problems. Not even a year earlier the woods were home to a vicious killer brought back from extinction. In "The Wolf's Moon," Mark Lansdowne and his pal, Warren Skruggs, sent them back…but at a cost. Now something is haunting the rivers in Crawford County. The Missouri State Water Patrol must solve the deaths of several residents who died in “The River” but can they stop this menace before more people are killed?
description: About the Author

Pat Jones was born and raised in St. Louis, Missouri. His special interests include the science of paleoanthropology and archaeology. Woodworking is one of his favorite hobbies, with special emphasis on the unique grains and textures of various species of trees. He and his wife, Sandy, thrive on designing and creating a flower garden of perennials, second to none! Constantly evolving, the garden began as a way that he could surprise his wife on her birthday. The rest is history! The garden now spans one fourth of an acre! When their children graduated from school, the couple relocated to rural Missouri where they now reside with their four dogs. The love of the area, in combination with the uniqueness of the people, provided the impedance for "The Wolf's Moon". A short story, "The River," followed shortly thereafter. The sequel to "The Wolf's Moon" is already in the works and proves to be yet another suspenseful page-turner! Pat believes that there is a story in everything. Everybody that he meets has their own special story; one simply has to take the time to listen. The story then writes itself. title: The Essential Guide to Being Polish: 50 Facts & Facets of Nationhood
features: Being Polish is no joke. For ten million people of Polish ancestry in the United States, as well as many who have settled in the UK since the fall of communism, it is a heartfelt matter⎯and amid all the travel guides and guides to Polish language, folklore, and customs, there is no single, comprehensive, reader-friendly and yet ever-informative reference on what it means to be Polish.

Enter The Essential Guide to Being Polish⎯the go-to concise resource for anyone looking to reconnect with their culture or, indeed, hoping that their friends, children, or colleagues learn something about their heritage.

Divided into three sections to make for an easy-to-follow format⎯Poland in Context, Poles in Poland, and Poles Abroad⎯this guide covers just about everything and does so in a style that is at once entertaining and informative: the country’s history and geography, wars, Jews in Poland, the communist past, the post-communist past and present, language, kings and queens, religion/Catholicism (with special focus on Pope John Paul II), holidays, food, and drink. What is a real Polish wedding all about? That, too, is addressed succinctly and with flair in this guide. Other chapters cover literature, music, art, famous scientists, Polish men and Polish women, Poles in America, Poles in the UK, Poles and the EU, and last but not least, Polish pride.

“[A] carefully researched but reader-friendly peregrination through the story of Poland―a thrilling if sometimes depressing ride you wouldn't believe if you read it in a novel. . . . I can say honestly . . . that The Essential Guide to Being Polish will not disappoint.” ―Krakow Post

“Do you plan to visit Poland for the first time? Are you contemplating a return trip? Do you enjoy reading about other countries and their cultures? If you answered ‘yes’ to any of the above then you must read The Essential Guide to Being Polish. . . . Once you start reading, you’ll want to read it all.” ―Am-Pol Eagle
“I invite you on this journey into the depths of the Polish soul.” ―from the Foreword by Lech Walesa, former President of Poland

About the Author

Anna Spysz, who is both the coauthor and the book's editor, is the former editor-in-chief of the Krakow Post (May 2008-December 2010), Poland's only English-language newspaper. A Polish-born American, she graduated in 2004 from the University of Texas at Austin with a BA in English and subsequently moved to Krakow, Poland, where she earned an MA in Central and Eastern European Studies from Jagiellonian University. She currently lives in Portland, Oregon. Her website is www.annaspysz.com.

Marta Turek moved from Poland to the United States as child with her parents, settling first in Chicago and, later, in Seattle. In 1993 she moved back to Poland, where she has been ever since. She has edited English-language texts and taught English as a second language for the past decade on both sides of the Atlantic. Her employers have ranged from ELS Language Centers in Seattle to schools, international companies, and universities in Poland. The holder of an MA in English linguistics from Adam Mickiewicz University in Poznań, she lives in Rokietnica, Poland.

Enter The Essential Guide to Being Polish⎯the go-to concise resource for anyone looking to reconnect with their culture or, indeed, hoping that their friends, children, or colleagues learn something about their heritage. Divided into three sections to make for an easy-to-follow format⎯Poland in Context, Poles in Poland, and Poles Abroad⎯this guide covers just about everything and does so in a style that is at once entertaining and informative: the country's history and geography, wars, Jews in Poland, the communist past, the post-communist past and present, language, kings and queens, religion/Catholicism (with special focus on Pope John Paul II), holidays, food, and drink. review_samples.title: Very good!
review_samples.text: In Knife, the fairy community of Oakenwyld our heroine belongs to is steadily declining, the people dying out. While the outside human world progresses in its technology and methods, the fairies in the Oak do not move forward or make any attempt, and sometimes even go backwards. Perhaps this has something to do with the loss of their magic many years ago during the Sundering, an event which also led to older fairies dying from a sickness known as the Silence, something that was never seen before the Sundering. When Knife is appointed as the Oak's hunter, a position that allows her to travel outside the Oak, she takes it upon herself to find a way to save her people. Then Knife meets Paul McCormick, the son of two humans living in the House opposite the fairies' Oak. I really liked the development of the relationship between her and Paul. For one thing it's quite unconventional and, because of the Oakenwyld's history, any contact with humans is feared, and that in itself makes it an interesting situation. Through Paul, Knife learns that humans aren't what the Oakenwyld makes them out to be and that, somehow, they are a key to saving her people. Knife is a very frank, practical and no-nonsense type of character. Unlike many young adult books I felt I could empathize with her and understood why she took the actions she made. The pacing of the story was very fine in my opinion, a sort of one-thing-leads-to-another scenario that ties up nicely, despite the information overload near the end. I had to flip back and forth to figure out what was happening there, but it all made sense in the end. The book doesn't lack for vivid descriptions; everything is outlined and drawn out in its own special way, and all of Knife's characters are quite developed, though I felt Amaryllis' performance wasn't quite up to par to what R. J. Anderson wanted to portray. Knife is a fun and unconventional fairy tale with original characters (and one strange name, but it grows on you) and an interesting premise. The story might not be completely original, but its execution is decent in its own right. I forward to reading the sequel, Rebel, and the third book which will tie up the trilogy in 2011.

SO MANY MORE DESIGNS

description: ALL CLANS ARE AVAILABLE.

This beautiful sterling silver or gold pendant combines an intricate Celtic cross background with your Clan crest mounted in the center. The Clan crest is exquisitely handcrafted and is 11/16" (19.5 mm) in diameter while the very detailed Celtic cross is 1-3/16" (30mm) square. The sterling silver pendant includes an 18" sterling silver box link chain. In gold a chain is available at an extra charge. Please inquire. This piece is crafted in high quality sterling silver, 10K and 14K yellow or white gold.
A wonderful way to display your proud Scottish Clan heritage.

The Clan crest is surrounded by a detailed belt and buckle design upon which is inscribed your Clan motto in raised relief lettering. In ancient times, the chief of the Clan presented to his Clansmen his crest for them to wear as a symbol of their loyalty and Clan affiliation.  We make our Clan designs by the “lost wax casting” process, which allows us to carve our master designs deeper in wax than would be possible with simple metal engraving. Each piece is painstakingly made by hand and the difference in the quality of design is significant. These are the finest detailed Clan crests available in the world! Our company has been in the Scottish Clan crest business for over forty one years. We are now making Clan and other Scottish jewellery for the children and grandchildren of our original customers!.

title: Women’s Handmade Adjustable Silk Multi Strand Necklace with Non-Precious Bead Accents, Buttons and Hand Dyed Yarns- LRW DESIGNS
features: Each one is handmade by textile designer Lynn Reiter Weinberg in her GA. Studio using upcycled hand painted silk fabrics from her years designing the Silkscapes and Lrw Designs clothing collections. Creations by LRW DESIGNS feel like you are draping a piece of artwork around your neck. It feels like a rich painting of bold hues.

Sophisticated jewel tones gracefully layer to form this simple yet sublime handmade necklace. The beauty is in the details. This innovative hand crafted multi strand design is graceful and sculptural and adds a dash of artistry to any look, whether you are dressing up a casual ensemble or adding the finishing touch to something special.

There is a filigree metal 1.5” diameter medallion that is handwoven with a hand dyed ribbon and accented with a bead in the center. The 3 strands dangle from the medallion and are made of hand painted silk, beads hand knotted on hand dyed yarns and recycled buttons. The opposite side has rings wrapped in hand painted silk.
For versatility the back has an adjustable bead closure, so you can determine what length works best depending on the outfit you are wearing.

Due to the diversity of the hand painted silks, beads and hand dyed yarns items will vary slightly in coloration. This makes each necklace a unique creation. Length adjusts from 14- 20 “ Hand wash cold, spot or dry clean

review_samples.title: These work for me!
review_samples.text: I bought these earrings because I needed something easy to put in, and that needs no backing to stay in. They look good! Simple and pretty! I have small plump earlobes, and my piercing is in the middle of my earlobe. The piercing is not a big hole, and is not droopy because I never wear heavy earrings. That's why I needed earrings that were easy to put in without twisting them apart and then needing to push them back in shape after finally getting them on. Then you do the same thing again to get them off. I had to return that TYPE of earring because it wore me out and hurt my ears, because of all the pulling. THESE are NOT like that. These are EASY! I've had neuropathy in my fingers that stops me from being able to use backings, because I can't feel if it even got on to the back of the earrings! These 13mm just go in easy and don't require backings, even though they include them if you think you need them. I didn't. A person that gave a negative review of these saying they look like a cut off paperclip! That does NOT do justice to these earrings! They do NOT look like that! These are for adults and teens, and children alike. There was no age group given in the ad, so just because they're small don't relegate them to just children! They are small. I WANTED small. They are about a half inch long. The space between the posts is just what I needed to just slip them in. No struggle! 18 gauge is not a thick post. When I put them in you can see in my picture that the bottoms don't extend very far below my earlobe. I pinched the bottoms a bit to be sure they would not come out as I cannot handle backings. They are comfortable and I don't even know they're there. I've worn them a couple days now. I've slept with them. They did not get caught in my night hat that I wear over my ears to keep my head warm and block out LED lights from my clock. I've even showered with them in and had no issues. These work for me because of all the above reasons. Thank you designer's! Money well spent!

title: The Space Needle Of Seattle Beautifully Upcycled Dictionary Page Book Art Print
description: This is an upcycled print printed on an old dictionary page. We take old books about to be destroyed and upcycle them in order to give them new life. The aging, slightly-yellowed page is carefully removed, and the image is printed directly on the recycled paper. The result is a unique and absolutely beautiful print suitable for framing. These prints are definite conversation-starters and look just gorgeous while hanging on the wall. The pages are approximately 8.5 x 11 in size, with a very slight variation. No two are exactly the same, but all will fit nicely in an 8.5 x 11 frame. You will not get the exact dictionary page shown in the image, but you will get a print from the same book. Every piece is original. ***Frame is not included****. You will receive just the print. These vintage book prints make awesome, unique gifts and are environmentally responsible. All prints are shipped flat in rigid, stay-flat mailers and are protected in plastic sleeves.

title: Regal Dog Products Medium Orange Reflective Dog Collar with Custom Engraved Name Plate and Heavy Duty Center Ring | Waterproof Biothane Personalized Dog Collars - Other Sizes for Small & Large Dogs
features: SAFETY UNDER SUNDOWN - Walking your dog in the dark is dangerous. Fetch some safety for both you and your furry friend with the Black Reflective Dog Collar by Regal Dog Products! As cars pass, the highly reflective strip notifies drivers of your presence so they can safely steer clear. Keep your dog visible and out of harm's way wherever you may go day or night. With the customizable name plate, you can keep your furry friend safe and properly idenfied.

UNCATCH YOUR CANINE - Not only does the reflective strip on the reflective dog collar keep your pet safe, but so does the innovative center ring! If your dog gets caught on a fence or branch, the center ring allows your dog to relieve pressure from their throat until rescue can arrive. It also serves as a handy spot to attach your matching leash or harness.

DOGGONE DURABLE - Poorly made dog collars often break the first time your pooch lunges for a squirrel, but this thick dog collar is designed to endure it all! The D ring and doube buckle are solid metal (not pliable plastic like other collars). Strong Buckle D Ring supports pull of 600 lb. Innovative coated nylon material provides extra durability for even the most active dogs; stands up to all weather, terrains and is virtually indestructible.

DOGGY PADDLE AWAY - Got a dog that likes to take a dive? Don't come home with a soggy, smelly pet collar. Instead, return home smelling fresh(er) when your dog wears this waterproof and odorless hunting dog collar! Vinyl-coated webbing on this waterproof dog collar is more durable than plastic, nylon or rubber dog collars. The non-cloth material never absorbs water so it stays dry and clean! Perfect for your beach bound pooch or hunting dog.

SIMPLY FETCHING - Give your dog some style with Regal Dog Products' cool dog collars! Our synthetic material is military grade and will hold up to the toughest outdoor conditions., and it has the sophisticated look and feel of leather minus the animal product. Plus, it keeps your pup comfy thanks to its adjustable, flexible, temperature-resistant design!

review_samples.title: SO CUTE!!!
review_samples.text: I’ve included a couple pictures for reference - one of the pendant and one of Sir Hammond the Handsome himself. So I actually really love this necklace! Cat and dog themed gifts are easy to come by but if your beloved companion is a less common beasty it can be hard to find items like this and I was really excited to find a hamster pendant. This little hamster shaped piece of metal with the little heart cut out detail and my big guy’s name engraved on it is adorable. A. Dor. A. ble. The overall shape of the pendant is spot on as well (that stubby little tail!) and It seems to be very sturdy. I truly do love it. So why the two stars? Well, first and foremost it’s completely overpriced. $35 for the pendant and a 16” necklace (which is like tiny choker size) puts the total cost at $50. I wasn’t really bothered by the price at first because its the only one like it I’ve found and I totally love it. However about 2-3 days into wearing it my neck and chest started itching terribly and a nice red rash developed everywhere the pendant and necklace touched my skin (I’m really sensitive to cheap metals). The pendant itself had also become very tarnished. normally I would return something with this many issues (particularly at this price point) but I really truly do love this necklace so I bought a new sterling silver chain on Amazon (which set me back like eight bucks) and polished the pendant to buff out the tarnished areas. In order to keep it from immediately tarnishing again and from further irritating my skin I used a thin coat of my clear gel nail polish (the kind that needs to be cured with a UV light) and this has kept it tarnish free ever since. So only two stars because at $50 I really shouldn’t have to go to such lengths just to be able to use an item as it’s intended. I’m stubborn though and I enjoy problem solving and I love my necklace enough that I was willing to put in the extra effort to keep it. I can’t really give it a higher rating though :(

review_samples.title: Beautiful sticker that adds character
review_samples.text: This really is a beautiful decal / sticker! It was easy to apply - I did it during my lunch break and it took me about 15 minutes from start to finish including cleaning off the rear window. For anyone having trouble with it, the trick is doing LOTS of rubbing with the edge of a credit card and then peeling the backing off very slowly. Even the tiny dots in the design stuck nicely. It's actually easy to see "through" when driving so it doesn't present a driving hazard. It's beautiful and really adds a nice bit of character to my silver car, making it easier to spot in a crowded parking lot as well!

review_samples.title: Feels like a scam honestly- Do not buy unless you're willing to fix it up yourself
review_samples.text: It's a long one, sorry- (TL:DR- You can make something better for the same price at a craft store) So I was lucky enough to find the $10 version of this exact product because the quality of this isn't worth any more than that. The reason I feel this is a scam is because I receive a page error when I go to the version that I bought and there wasn't an "Only 1 left" note before purchasing. I would consider this a "third-party, homemade" thing if it weren't for the 7 other differently priced listings with the exact same thing under different companies. The fabric was loosely and unevenly hot glued, and a lot of cardboard was exposed. I ended up taking out the damaged cardboard (damaged because this was delivered in a bag rather than a box and arrived bent out of shape), sewed up the wings and stuffed them with polyfill. I won't post a picture because I don't want them to use it to trick people further but I promise that stuffing the wings is much better. Buy with caution.

The Palace of Westminster, also known as the House of Parliament or Westminster Palace, in London, is where the two houses of the Parliament of the United Kingdom (the House of Lords anf the House of Commons) meet. The palace lies on the north bank of the River thames in the London borough of the City of Westminster, close to the government buildings of Whitehall. The magnificent Gothic Revival masterpiece you see today was built between 1840 and 1888, this was thework of Charles Barry who designed the buildings to blend with nearby Westminster Abbey. The two imposing towers, well known landmarks in London, are the clock tower, named after it's thirteen ton bell called Big Ben, and Victoria tower, on whose flag pole the Union jack flien when parliament is sitting. Much of the Victorian detail of the interior was the work of Barry's assistant Augustus Pugin. The Clock Tower is a focus on New Year celebrations in hte United Kingdom, with radio and television stations tuning to its chimes to welcome the start of the year. During the second world war in 1941, an incendiary bomb destroyed the Commons chamber of the Houses of Parliament, but the clock tower remained intact and Big Ben continued to keep time and trike away at the hours, its unique sound was broadcast to the nation and around the world, a welcome reassurance of hope to all who heard it.

review_samples.title: Fun Item.
review_samples.text: Fun compact piece. Not too bulky so fits most places just fine. My daughter loves it.

review_samples.title: Perfect Foam Ballpit
review_samples.text: I am loving this ball pit for my two year old! Upon taking it out of the box and shrink wrapping, it sprung up pretty instantly. The instructions said to let it fully find its shape for about 3 days, but honestly it looked pretty great as soon as I opened it. The extent of assembly is just placing a large foam circle into the bottom of the pit so that it holds the form. I really enjoy the stretch to the fabric. It's great for kids diving in and out of it and I don't imagine you would need to worry about it ripping. Be aware that this pit is fairly large and will require multiple packs of plastic balls to fill. They can be a little pricey for what they are and that cost could add up. Over all though, it's a great toy for your kids, is aesthetically pleasing, and holds up well!

review_samples.title: It’s a huge hit with my 12mo old granddaughter!
review_samples.text: My granddaughter loves ball pits. She had a collapsible type but was always climbing out of it and flattening the walls. With this one, the walls are more stable and the memory foam bounces right back. It didn’t take long to fully inflate and we waited 24 hours before adding balls. She loves it and so do her parents. Only wish is that it was bigger!

review_samples.title: Decent Construction... But Incomplete
review_samples.text: This foam ball pit is of a decent size, and it appears capable of standing up to the rough and tumble play of toddlers. Of the foam ball pits we've had (this is number three) this is likely the best constructed, with appropriately fitted soft fabric and smooth walls; however, for what it is this product is incredibly expensive. No balls are included with the product, which means anyone purchasing this ball pit can expect to pay another $70 at minimum (for Amazon brand balls that are used... expect more around $100+ for new balls) to get enough plastic balls to make this product functional as a ball pit. Ultimately, you will have to pay a total of $150 to $200 to actually put this thing to use as a ball pit. That is far too expensive for a product of this type, particularly when there are alternatives in the market that include balls for less than that $150 price point. At the end of the day, a product of this type feels like it should carry a price tag well under $50, The fact this is marked up to around $76 makes it very unappealing when considering the alternatives in the marketplace. In conclusion, you'd be better off looking for a ball pit of this type that includes the plastic balls... and then wait for it to go on sale. Odds are you will be able to find such a product for substantially less than $100, which saves you money and saves you the time of having to hunt down balls after the fact. Overall, this product earns 4/5 stars for being better than its counterparts... but too expensive and incomplete.

review_samples.title: Very Thematic Medieval Story Game!
review_samples.text: Oltree is a game that caught my eye because of the art and theme. I was able to get in two plays before this review. We played the starting short scenario and the Dragon Scenario. The starting scenario was a good place to start as it wasn’t long but quickly showed us what we were doing wrong for future games. It’s nice that they included this scenario to give you a chance to learn the game or to play if you don’t have an hour or more to play. The game has a lot of thematic text about your adventures and sucks you into the game the first few times (overtime the text does feel a bit generic). It reminds me a bit of Arkham Horror 2e with how you interact with location. You have to manage the amount of “interactions” at a location sort of like Pandemic, not wanting to have too many at one spot but if you clear them all and have a castle tower built you secure that location. This mechanic is a bit less punishing and easier to manage than in Pandemic. These story elements are fun but I wish there was a bit more choice and punishment for failing the interaction. Most interactions, even if you fail them don’t have anything bad happen it seems. The game does have multiple “decks” that you use for these interactions and are paired with the Story for that game. So the Interaction Decks you use do change for each game making each Story you play through feel more unique. Now the Story of the game is quite an interesting mechanic. I really love how thematic it is! As you play the story will slowly progress and change. Each time you play a story for the first time is very interesting and fresh. I really hope they make expansions to expound on this feature. After playing through the story one or two times though I can see how the excitement could wear off and you will easily learn what to expect to happen next. An advantage to this is you’ll be able to play the game more strategically and if it gets “too easy” you can always increase the difficulty of the game. There are three difficulty levels; easy, medium, and hard. When I played I played on medium each time and lost everytime just slightly. Though I have yet to repeat a story. My biggest frustration with how the story worked is it didn’t give you any indication (as far as I noticed) to what you would need to do to beat the story. One of them we got to the end and it was purely based on rolling dice in a specific profession (or skill). It was a very anti-climatic ending as there was nothing we could do to prepare for this event and we lost just one not having enough dice. If we knew a bit more what the story expected we could have prepared slightly better. But now we will know for the next time we replay that specific story. I haven’t played through more than two stories yet so I am not sure how different they will be. It does seem like each story will be very unique and will most likely have slightly different ways to finish the story. Some stories have branching storylines, which the ones we played happened to not have that mechanic. When I can get the game to the table again with my group I’ll try to update this review. I think sometimes the game can feel overly simple. You get basically 4 actions to choose from and can perform two a turn. Move, Interact with a location (interaction, problem, or call on community), Build, or Rest. Since most characters can’t perform two of the same actions in a row most of the game feels like you’re only doing one interesting action along with a move action to either get to where you want to be or to prepare for your next turn. The turns are quick and simple though which is nice because the game keeps moving along pretty quickly without having to worry about much analysis paralysis from other players. Our first time playing a “Long” story took us roughly 1:22 with three people and I am sure that time can very easily be cut down to 45-60 min once everyone knows how to play. The components to this game are really nice, they used wood for the resource tokens, character pawns, and a few other things. The Characters all have a unique wooden horse pawn with screen printed art on them. The pieces that are cardboard are thick and not cheap. The art is very well done and not distracting from game play but actually enhances it well. The production quality for this game is really good. I do enjoy this game. It’s easy to teach, fun to play, and doesn’t last too long at the table. The game will really need some expansions to keep the game feeling fresh as you will quickly play through all the included stories multiple times within 10 plays. I did see it has one expansion planned but has not yet been released at the time of writing this review. What I like: - Quality components - Thematic game play - Beautiful art - Simple but effective box organization - Not analysis paralysis prone - Good play length What I didn't Like: - Story could hint at how to win a bit more - Turns can feel overly simple/short - Location Interactions fails not punishing enough (though some might think this is good) - Stories will get repetitive quickly (a few good expansions will help keep the game fresh)

review_samples.title: Hard knocks to the rulebook
review_samples.text: My biggest complaint for this game is the rulebook. We did not find it to be very well written and it made what is a fairly simple game into one that was more confusing than it needed to be. There are how to play videos available online and I would recommend watching one to get at least an overview before slogging through the rules. It's not complicated, but again... the rulebook is not the best read. The game itself is not bad. The narrative aspect is the best part in my opinion but not as interesting as it could have been. The events tend to become repetitive. There are several decks of cards and you mix up a couple of them depending on what scenario you're doing to give a somewhat different experience for each scenario. Scenarios come in short, medium and long so you can pick an appropriate one for the time that you have to play. The production of the game is extremely nice. The screen printed meeples, cards and player boards are very nice. The insert is very cute but has one big failing in that you need to bag your cards/components otherwise they slide into the other compartments. This kind of defeats the purpose of the compartments. I wish I could give it a 3.5 but no half stars are allowed. So 5 stars for the components, 2 stars for the rulebook (ease of learning), and 3.5 for the gameplay itself.

review_samples.title: A bit pumpkin shaped, but your little spider-fan likely won't care.
review_samples.text: These non-licensed Spider-Hero inspired (inSPIDERed amirite?!) beach balls as exactly what you'd expect, maybe less leaning on the lower end of quality akin to a not to round dollar store beach ball. Comes in a pack of 3 and you'll need it. Also has a few sticker patches included if you want to try to find the leaks. The air definitely doesn't hold as we had all 3 left out inflated, the next day they've already lost some air. Not sure if the issue is the plug itself or bag seams but truthfully I should expect these as a limited time item anyway. Its only matter of time before either the wind blows it off into oblivion or one of your little ones sits on it for a full spider-burst. The shape is also odd, the panels seam to form a hexagon shape and when filled its more pumpkin leaning than sphere. You may hear someone cry out that its not regulation in your pro beach ball sports leagues. Not that it matters, your spider-fans will be too hyped up to grab it to notice. If you have a spider-obsessed little roommate, you can slap those signature eyes on anything red and they'll go bananas. The house of mouse charges a premium but for something as trivial as a beach ball, "Spider hero" may be the way to go. 3 stars - cheap (in both the good and bad way). If we ignore the unlicensed Spider-Face, its a below average 2 star not so spherical beach ball. Update - Added new photo. Yeah the seams are terrible on these, felt the need to drop it to 2 stars. Don't understand the high reviews at all, almost as if people who are getting it for free are just dropping 5 stars undeservedly. I was content they were cheap and bootleg but even dollar store beach balls will last more than a couple weeks. RIP Spidey balls.

review_samples.title: My go-to for my Rings
review_samples.text: I absolutely love Solarez products, I own many of their different UV resins and use this specific one for my ring protective tops whenever I can! It's cures crystal clear, hard, quick (~3 minutes), and polishes up real nice after sanding if needed. Highly recommend this for jewelry and check out their recommendations on how to cure the resin. Look it up - don't quote me, but blast it with a quick UV exposure, wait a minute for the initial reaction to cool down (don't touch - it'll be tacky!), then do spurts - on, off, on, off- every other second of exposure for the rest of the 3 minutes(?) definitely look it up on their website for tips. REGULAR BLACK LIGHTS DO NOT WORK! That's your PSA - Solarez sells a 385nm UV light on amazon that works amazingly well and/or sunlight, or sunlamp work. Good luck and happy crafting!

review_samples.title: The Review to Guarantee My Entrance Into Geekdom
review_samples.text: Okay, I admit it, I am a nerd. Okay I said it...what a relief...I'm glad I got this off my chest now I don't have to keep living a lie. I have been entranced by Star Wars since I first saw it in 1977. I wasn't even in my teens yet. After the movie I just sat there in my seat completely mesmerized. My dad stood up, "C'mon, Johnny...let's go..." I just kept looking into space, "Dad, my life is never going to be the same...ever..." Yoda is my favorite character. Always has been. Always will be. Even when I first saw him in the Empire Strikes back, I knew on a subconscious level of things, that he exuded everything that I wanted to be: wise, compassionate, insightful, childlike, and very, very strong...not physically, but mentally, emotionally, and spiritually...he was alligned to Something greater than he and let it flow through him. We geeks like to call this 'the Force' but you can call it Energy, Universal Intelligence, or maybe even God... I consider myself a very spiritual being. I meditate, I pray, I immerse myself in Spiritual books, tapes, and movies and my Spirituality has seeped its way into every aspect of my life. I am not a closet believer. I do believe in a Divine Intelligence that binds and holds everything together, just like Obi Wan said in the 1977 movie that started it all. And even though I believe that all of us are Spiritual Beings and are basically masters trapped in neophyte bodies, there have been some that have allowed this Power to move through them, as them. Think Jesus, Buddah, Krishna, Yoda...yes, Yoda...and because I believe that Yoda is an ascended master he is on my altar along with other deities that encompass the things I joyfully strive to bring forth. This is a great representation and belongs on every serious Star Wars fanatics shelf. It's not some cheap little model or some plastic, goofy representation. It's very authentic looking and embodies Yoda's wisdom and his heart. I do not consider it "an idol" or a "graven image"...my old religious training coming out...I see it as a gentle reminder to practice those things that add rather than take away from the human experience. Well, I'm gonna go now and play with my Yoda...I mean, I'm going to meditate and reflect on the Inner power within me... Have a day filled with blessings and May the Force Be With You... Yes. I am a geek.

review_samples.text: This was a gift for my boss purchased mis November for Christmas. Instead of minimal problems beyond a little wait with shipping, this item was returned to sender after barely being shipped on time. When asked for a refund and cancellation the seller refused, so I had to wait another month for this item to finally arrive. It arrived used, torn open, and squashed, with wear and tear that wouldn't be seen on an item that may have just had a bumpy ride in post. Seller provided poor communication so I had to contact Amazon regarding this problem. Once finally out of box and turned on, the item is janky and poorly made, little more then a nick knack that'll be used once for the novelty and then thrown away due to quality. Doesn't even drop coins into the box without physical assistance and can stutter on endlessly.

review_samples.text: My son is 7 months old and we thought maybe he will be able to play with it. Well they seem pretty spot on with the age appropriation so he will be there soon. My older kids love showing him how to pop the characters up. It has a nice volume of music, not overwhelming loud like some I heard. It appears to be very durable, my kids have dropped it a couple times and it still works fine. My infant loves looking at the lights bounce around from character to character. Really like it!

review_samples.title: Eggsceptional eggsciting developmental toy!
review_samples.text: A must-have to add to your arsenal of fundamental toys. It’s amazing how little minds grow and thrive when given opportunities such as this. So happy to have found this for my grand baby. Love everything about this toy. From the carrying handle to the quiet mode and everything else in between. There are a total of 5 animals…a push, flip, turn, press and pull which makes this product all the more valuable and worthwhile, as opposed to other similar product that had only 4.

review_samples.title: So much fun and has different stages
review_samples.text: This is a great baby toy as it has so many things to do and brightly colored animals. It has 3 stages, 1 is no sound just play with the pop up buttons, 2 plays music and animal sounds while baby plays, or 3 has a light up feature for baby to follow along with. I really enjoy this toy!

review_samples.title: Great Cause and Effect Toy
review_samples.text: [[VIDEOID:c44de88647ced2aeb6ee4c78a005fb87]] My 2.5 year old and almost 11 month old fight over this toy, so I actually have 2 of these. My 2.5 year old (who has all but been officially diagnosed with ASD) is finally just starting to take interest in more complex toys and he loves this thing! I would absolutely recommend this!

review_samples.title: Easy to Drive, Not Durable
review_samples.text: My toddler and preschooler really enjoy this excavator. It's fun to drive and rather easy for younger children to navigate the remote. It is mostly plastic though so I don't see the arm and bucket being very durable for the long run. We've already had to rubber band the arm after my son picked it up by the arm instead of the base.

review_samples.title: Metal bucket, rest of it is mostly plastic
review_samples.text: Pros, Likes, and Features * Full function forward and reverse with turning on the base and then the arm goes up and down and scoop goes in and out just like a real excavator *Has a metal scoop, the rest is mostly plastic *Comes with 2 batteries * works well, fun to play with in sand but rocks, gravel, dirt not so much Cons *Mostly plastic, don't see this lasting very long * Doesn't work well in dirt, works ok in sand and is fun for the kids, adults not so much.. *Doesn't come with a charging block for charging, must use another usb charging block *Not worth leaving the screw for battery door in on the tractor, battery doen't last a long time so with 2 you need to be able to switch it out easier. With that this is mostly plastic so I don't see it lasting too long. Works great in sand but not so much with gravel, rocks, and dirt. It doesn't have a charging block like most items anymore so have to use another charging block. And the final though is the screw for the battery door. As many times as you'll need to change out the battery, you might as well remove it because its more a headache than a need at this point. Maybe put the screw in it when you put it up only..

title: BMC Marx Plastic Army Men Beach Assault - Green vs Tan 24pc WW2 US Soldiers - Made in USA
features: BMC Classic WWII United States Soldiers
Colors: OD Green and Tan

Scale: Approximately 1:32

description: From the CLASSIC ARMY MEN COLLECTOR SERIES, BMC Toys brings back an iconic set of figures from the Golden Age of Army Men Playsets. This pack of 24 Olive Drab and Tan WW2 US Soldier PLASTIC ARMY MEN is proudly manufactured in the United States and features 5 different figures and rafts. Troops are approximately 1:32 scale, stand up to 2.1 inches tall, and are made from flexible tan and olive drab green color LDPE plastic with good details and a little flashing. Each color includes 4 seated Marines, 4 Oarsmen, 2 Landing Craft Rubber Boat (LCR), 2 Paratroopers in 2 poses, and instructions for easy to make parachutes from paper napkins and thread. The raft measures 5.5 inches long, is hollow underneath, and even floats on water. These figures were originally produced around 1960 by Louis Marx & Company and were included in many of their famous Battleground and History in the Pacific Playsets. They were also offered in playsets by various companies through the 1980s and 1990s, and later produced in hard plastic for the hobby market. These are excellent troops for a variety of set ups from WW2 to Cold War conflicts. This is a set of real American Made plastic heroes, meant to be set up, knocked down, picked up and played with for many years to come. LITTLE GREEN ARMY MEN have even been inducted into the National Toy Hall of Fame. Packed in plastic bag with insert card and recommended for ages 5 and up. title: AMIGO None of a Kind Brainteaser, Party & Family Game
features: AGES 7+ | 2-6 PLAYERS
A NEW KIND OF “MATCHING” GAME: Challenge your brain to create a pattern that DOESN’T match!

HOW TO PLAY: Players race to build a row where adjacent cards share no matching attributes – color of the word, color of the ink, & number of words on the card. It may sound easy, but it's surprisingly challenging.

HELPS IMPROVE YOUR BRAIN’S PROCESSING SPEED: Ever heard of the “Stroop Test”? None of a Kind is based on this famous psychology experiment that has been proven to help the brain work faster–it helps with skills like multi-tasking and executive functioning.
INCLUDES: 80 Linen-finish Color Cards, 30 Linen-finish Point Cards, Illustrated Instructions
description: Wait—it says "blue," but it's printed in red. What's going on? This multi-player brainteaster game is designed to befuddle, and strenghten your brain. Everyone plays at once as you race to match up cards that don't match—it sounds easy, but it's surprisingly challenging. None of a Kind is based on The Stroop Test, one of the most-cited papers in experimental psychology. It studies the relationship between the brain’s processing speed and executive functions, focusing on regions of the brain involved in planning, decision-making, and managing real-world interference, such as multi-tasking. In other words, playing None of a Kind improves your brain’s processing speed!

review_samples.title: I AM IRON MAN
review_samples.text: I got this when it first came out - my second figure ( after Batman ) love the MARK VII suit. Only issue I have is the pose is just a little too symmetrical. Would have liked to see his hands open defending ( but other versions are posed that way ) The build quality is great and the light up features are nice. GREAT PAINT APPLICATION - nice base - overall it's a fantastic figure to own. Love it.

review_samples.title: Great statue could have been even better
review_samples.text: This Kotobukiya Iron Man "statue" (even the box itself states it is a model) is well sculpted and the detail is terrific. Very solid paint job as well, and the light up eyes and chest are a real nice addition. So why not five stars? Well here is why... 1: The plastic figure feels cheap. When I was assembling it I was worried I was going to break it. Especially when I was trying to attach the upper torso to the lower body. It is difficult to attach and I kept waiting for the figure to break. 2: The box shows Iron Man with his hands open, repulsors ready to go. The figure itself has Iron Man with closed fists. How awesome it would have been to have the lighted effect featured on his open-handed repulsors. 3: I paid about $60, but I see them regularly selling for around $100. I am sorry, but for that kind of money I expect a true statue sculpted out of more durable materials. This piece seems overpriced to me. My review may seem negative, I am trying to be impartial here. As a collector of Iron Man statues, I really do love the piece. I just feel like Kotobukiya had a chance to hit a home run with this sculpture, but fell short.

description: The Molymod MMS-009 inorganic/organic molecular model set for students in grades 7-12 includes 52 color-coded plastic atom parts and 37 links in a storage box. This set provides students a hands-on activity to visually model inorganic molecules, empirical formula representations, organic structures, and other concepts of inorganic and organic chemistry. Students can model molecules such as carbon dioxide, ammonia, sulfuric acid, calcium hydroxide, metal salts, copper sulfate, alkanes, alcohols, glucose, and benzene. The atom parts and links for assembling models are made from durable plastic and are color coded to national standards for ease of identification. Atom parts range from 17mm to 23mm in diameter and represent carbon, nitrogen, oxygen, hydrogen, sulfur, phosphorus, halogen, and metal. Additionally, it contains 4 brown atoms, 3 beige lone pair 2D paddles, 20 medium length grey links, 5 medium purple links, 12 flexible long grey links, one link remover tool, and instructions. The kit comes in a plastic box for ease of storage.

Science education products incorporate applied math and science principles into classroom and homeschool-based projects. Teachers in pre-K, elementary, and secondary classrooms use science education kits and products alongside science, technology, engineering, and math (STEM) curriculum to demonstrate STEM concepts and real-world applications through hands-on activities. Science education projects include a broad range of activities, such as practical experiments in engineering, aeronautics, robotics, energy, chemistry, physics, biology, and geology.

Spiring Enterprises manufactures molecular models for use in classrooms and educational settings under brands such as Molymod, miniDNA, and Molyorbital. Founded in 1967, the company is headquartered in Billingshurst, West Sussex, UK.

review_samples.title: Great Analog Cam Combo!
review_samples.text: [[VIDEOID:6b325883e5939ef32ce6405c540eee83]] These Spotter V2 cameras are the best bang for the buck. Durable for RC car rollovers & bashing. I also use to FPV drive RC cars & crawlers with Skyzone 04LV2 goggles. Simple combo unit with very decent lens. I have 3 of them. Inside and outside of RC model video is great. Be mindful of keeping airflow on the unit. The video (low res on box monitor, not goggles) has a cam on a Traxxas Maxx V2 bashing. This is my most beat-up cam of the 3 I have, & it's still working!

review_samples.title: Pretty inexpensive setup for FPV
review_samples.text: Quick and easy to set up and get shooting. Probably the most inexpensive and cost effective way to fly FPV as a beginner.

review_samples.title: My overall experience!
review_samples.text: This all in 1 FPV camera is one of the best I've used. I have brought other cheaper lower quality 3 in 1 FPV camera, and the wires will just short circuit, and would overheat easily. Not with this camera, plus it has a built in heatsink which helps a lot. My only and main complaint about this camera is that once I stick the servo connector to power this camera, when I tried to remove the connector, it won't budge. I ended up breaking the original servo connecter. Good thing I had spares to fix it. But it's important to be aware of that.

review_samples.title: Gets hot, but it's a cool fpv device easy to use
review_samples.text: Camera quality is a little shabby . But for a camera trasmitter combo it's worth buying. The quality is good enough to have a live view of your rc plane in the air. I haven't tried it for distance yet

review_samples.title: A great price but...
review_samples.text: I recently tried the TANSAR 7.5mm gel splatter balls with my GEL BLASTER STARFIRE gun, and while they come at a great price and quantity, I found that they don't perform as well as the Gel Blaster Gellets™ that came with my gun. Unfortunately, these gel balls tend to break apart when fired, which makes it difficult to maintain accuracy and results in a bit of a mess. While I appreciate the affordability of these gel balls, I wish they were of better quality to match their quantity. Overall, I'd recommend sticking with the Gel Blaster Gellets™ for a better shooting experience, but if you are on a budget these are still fun.

review_samples.title: Fun for hours!
review_samples.text: [[VIDEOID:6a4438cebeb4f3348d227e0f83ee9ffb]] This automatic gel ball blaster is really awesome. It is easy to put together and only takes 2 hours to fully charge. There is a light on the charger that indicates when it is done in green. This blaster does not light up but has a storage compartment for gel balls. There is an on/off button so you don't wear down the batteries. Make sure you grow your gel balls to the correct size or they will not work in the blaster. It is lightweight and easy to handle! Comes with a strap so it is easier to hold. Images and colors are clear and bright! Highly recommend!

review_samples.text: I'm not sure how long these will last as the clip and buttstock seem cheaply made. With that being said it is a neat alternative to a nerf gun and it works well as of now.

review_samples.title: Nice gel blaster
review_samples.text: This gel blaster is one of the best made ones on Amazon. The quality is great and it looks and feels great when holding. It's got great accuracy and the speed is really fast shooting the gel balls. It comes with a lot of accessories like aregular magazine,and extra gel balls as well as clear safety glasses. Comes all ready to assemble and install the battery and go have some awesome fun. Highly recommend as this one is built way better then a lot of the other gel blasters on Amazon. Can't go wrong with this one.

review_samples.title: Tons of fun with only a couple of minor quibbles
review_samples.text: This product is great fun to have with a little one. The cars are FAST! They stay on the track no matter the configuration as advertised. And with a little finagling they can climb walls, furniture and just about anything else. They can even go upside down. I only have a couple of minor issues with the product. First, plan to go through a LOT of batteries or invest in some decent rechargeables. I'd say that you'll be lucky to get an hour of non-stop play out of them before they need to be changed out and, quite honestly, you'll want to change them out before they completely die because the cars struggle with steep hills even before that. The cars also get a little hot after a lengthy play session. Nothing to worry about in terms of safety for your little ones' hands but something to note. On the other hand, one safety concern you do need to worry about is that the underside of the cars can pinch fingers pretty bad if you aren't careful. There are two sideways wheels that grip the middle portion of the track. It's what keeps the cars from falling off when they go up steep inclines or upside down. Those wheels are plastic and they spin very fast. If you get a finger stuck between them when handling the cars while they're on (turning them around, etc.), it can hurt a bit. I know from experience. I'd say that kids aged 5+ will have no problem understanding this and being careful but you could have problems with younger kids when playing. Just something to be aware of. You can also combine sets of these to make your tracks longer. One is fairly short. Two is the magic number in my opinion. Our gift recipient actually has four but you don't need that many unless you want to go through multiple rooms. Overall, great product with just a couple of minor issues to be mindful of. They're definitely a lot of fun.

description: Science goes glam with the You*niverse Ultimate Chemistry Lab! Have you ever wondered how crystals form? Or what makes something fizzy? You’ll learn these and much more when you put on your hot pink safety goggles and dive into the world of chemistry! This chemistry lab for kids lets you discover how science goes into some of your favorite things, including bath bombs, crystals and slime! With 20 different experiments to try, you’ll be fizzing, mixing and exploding your way to hours of fun. Follow the fully-illustrated instruction booklet to perform each experiment and gain a greater understanding of the science that’s occurring. From crystal-growing fuzzy sticks, to slime, and glow-in-the-dark test tubes—there’s an experiment for tons of thrilling scientific properties! Explore non-Newtonian fluids and polymer science while you discover what happens when different compounds mix—touch, feel, and watch the stages of matter in action! Chemistry gets a glow-up—literally—when you create your own glow sticks! This at-home chemistry kit allows you to learn about scientific principles and how chemistry is everywhere in the You*niverse! So go ahead, grab a pipette and a test tube, and get experimenting! Use the purple case as your experimentation station—the clear lid has all the spots to set up your equipment and serves as the perfect surface to conduct your experiments! When you’re done, keep everything in the storage container to stay organized and bring the chemistry lab on the road! Educational kits like this—and other You*niverse products—are an easy, fresh way to learn, all while having FUN! Recommended for aspiring chemists 6 years and up.

review_samples.title: Disney Princess Mulan Doll So Cheap!
review_samples.text: If you like a doll that is articulated (movable arms & legs) and has an adorable face with a nice outfit then this Disney Style Series 2 Mulan Doll is the one for an Adult Doll Collector or for your child to enjoy. This Mulan Disney doll by Hasbro is for the suggested ages of 6+. The doll box package arrived in great condition as there were no dents or any damage on the packaging. Mulan has a painted on face with real long black curled eyelashes. Mulan colorful outfit has a very thin see through sheer overlay with pink details. The doll dress material has a shimmer to it with various colors of purple, green and blue. The dress she is wearing underneath is somewhat of a light cranberry color with a blue thin ribbon tied on the outside of the top overlay. The dress and overlay color combination is very pretty and sparkly. Mulan is wearing plastic gold colored heel shoes with a plastic fan styled handbag on her wrist and she also is wearing a plastic flower headband. Mulan waist length jet black hair is easy to comb. The back of the box art drawing is adorable. The price for this doll was really cheap. If you can find this doll for under $20 you will have a nice doll for a really cheap price. I really like this doll. The doll does not come with a doll stand so if you plan to unbox the doll and want to display her, you will have to purchase one separately.

review_samples.title: These will get the job done, but are they for your best cards? Nah.
review_samples.text: These binders offer convenient side-loading, the strap is handy to keep the cover closed, and the binder cover is thick enough to protect the innards. Not sure I'd put my bestest in this binder, but for everyday cards, tokens, lands, your 2nd string stuff, I think these are super handy to keep that kind of stuff organized. They seem a little pricier than very similar binders you can find on Amazon. Do note they don't state that the card sleeves are archival quality. Will they really degrade your cards? Time will tell.

review_samples.title: great quality side loading binder
review_samples.text: This is a great binder, especially for the price point. It has a semi hard cover and back to help keep the cards inside safe. It is portfolio style uses black 9 slot pages which makes it easier to see the cards with the black color. They are also side loading so your cards will never fall out. I am using this to store pokemon cards and It's perfect for that, the cards fit in the slots perfectly with sleeves on and do not move around much if at all. Lastly it comes with an attached strap so you can close it tightly to again keep the cards inside safe, this is an excellent binder and for this price It's definitely worth stocking up on them if you are doing master sets or anything similar.

review_samples.title: Perfect for Pokémon
review_samples.text: This card holder is exactly what you need to keep your Pokémon cards in good condition. You can fit up 4 cards in each slot easily, so having doubles doesn’t mean you need to have a whole new slot. The black background makes it easier to see the cards as well.

title: Big Dot of Happiness Mardi Gras - Bar Bingo Cards and Markers - Masquerade Party Bingo Game - Set of 18
features: Masquerade Bingo Cards and Markers INCLUDES 18 game cards, 18 perforated marker sheets, 1 perforated call sheet, and game instructions.

MUST-HAVE PARTY SUPPLY: Bingo is an easy and classic Mardi Gras game that everyone will have fun playing. Masquerade Bingo Cards and Markers give this classic game a fresh look with Mardi Gras playing cards and activities related words instead of numbers.

HOW TO PLAY: Play traditional bingo rules or take out with your group and play bar bingo. Like gift bingo, bar bingo is played by observing your crowd and marking the space when you see a corresponding item. Begin traditional play by the designated bingo leader pulling a caller chip from the bowl. Each guest covers the called word on their card with square marker. Continue until a guest has covered a row in any direction – vertically, horizontally, or diagonally and calls out “BINGO!”.

Each card measures 5” Wide x 7” Tall, perforated marker sheets measure 2.75” Wide x 5” Tall and individual markers measure 0.75” Wide x 0.75” Tall.

MADE IN THE USA: Mardi Gras Bingo Game is designed and manufactured at our Wisconsin facility using materials that are Made in the USA. review_samples.title: Excelent designed 180/200 class heli
review_samples.text: This review is for the explorer version. This is a very well built and very well engineered heli. Not that it needed it but I took apart and inspected the main head before maiden flight. I just do that with all helis I don't initially put together my self. There was plenty of grease in the thrust bearings. The feathering shaft screws did need blue locktight. All other screws were tight and had either locktight or ca glue. I also replaced the carbon composit blade grips whith aluminum ones. I just like those better. Everything else is stock. I used a Frsky R-XSR receiver hooked into the Sbus port. And bound it to a Jumper T16 pro hall TX. (I also build and fly FPV freestyle quads so to me setup was easy) I wanted to use a "satellite" receiver so to take advantage of OpenTx programming. The OMP receiver I don't think will allow you to setup custom pitch and throttle curves and this is essential in tuning the flight characteristics to your liking. The main head components are smooth and tight. There is no play in the linkage at all. Very precision built. (I'm also a CNC machinist and programmer so I can appreciate the main head components fitting very precise) The motors are very high quality and very smooth running. The tail motor works very well. Super powerful and won't blow out on you. The direct drive main motor is a very good design and is smooth and quiet. All you hear is blade noise, and it sounds great in the air. I got 8 min flights just flying scale circuits with 3.70 ish resting Volts per cell. This heli flies smooth, stable and rock solid. It is as responsive as you like it to be and could be tamed down to be an excelent trainer if paired with a TX that has pitch and throttle curve programming. OMP Hobby did an excellent job with this one. I would not hesitate at all to pick this one up if you're looking for a 180 to 200 size heli. This heli way out performs my Trex 450 flybar clone.

review_samples.title: Tons of fun! Won't run well on uncarpeted floors. But that's OK.
review_samples.text: I haven't tried the smoke yet but everything else works great! Runs on carpet, grass, dirt and mud. The engine sounds are GREAT! Controls are easy to understand and intuitive. Battery and charger are great. Instructions are comprehensive and easy to understand. Turret rotates as advertised. The tank can easily negotiate obstacles. I have plans for a tank shooting range.in the yard with paper targets and scale figures. Machine gun looks and sounds great. Cannon "recoil" is VERY realistic. I'm going to buy some extra (better) batteries. This is a FUN tank. The plastic accessories are realistic and made to scale. Ammo cans, shovel, crates, spare parts, helmet, rucksack and more! I have zero complaints. Well worth the investment!

review_samples.text: This is an amazing tank. I have another tank that cost nearly twice as much as this one but when it comes time to play, I am always pulling this one out first. review_samples.title: Best RC tank yet.
review_samples.text: This thing is a beast. I have owned many 1/16 RC tanks from several different makers. By far this is the best. I have this one and the down graded one with plastic tracks. Both are superb tanks. I am pretty rough on these. I seal them with electrical tape and run them through soupy mud and they do great. (NOT ADVISED) I spent a ton of money on a full metal tiger from taigen a while back. It keeps throwing a track even on flat pavement. I have yet to have this throw a track even as hard as I run it. My only complaint is the controller. I had a lose wire I easily reattached in it. It ran well for a while. Now it will not power up. I am in the process of trouble shooting now.

review_samples.title: An excellent display model
review_samples.text: A well engineered kit that is mid-level for difficulty and skill, it is designed for modelers with some experience, not for beginners (their Snap Tite line is for beginners). Styrene cement, paints, and (if desired) foil for trim is not included. Basic modeling tools also required. Makes a great model "from the box" and can be outstanding with aftermarket or scratch-built detail additions. Priced fairly for what the buyer gets. Not particularly educational for an experienced modeler, durable only as a display model, not as a toy for children to play with.

title: Cool Maker - KumiFantasy Fashion Pack, Makes Up to 12 Bracelets with The KumiKreator, for Ages 8 and Up
features: SPIN TO CREATE: The Cool Maker KumiKreator is a breakthrough bracelet maker; it makes it so easy to create friendship bracelets without a single knot needed! Choose a bracelet design from the KumiFantasy design booklet, load the machine (sold separately) with the colorful spools and spin to create! As you turn the handle, you’ll be mesmerized as the spools dance around the machine, magically weaving your bracelet together in minutes!

MAKE UP TO 12 BRACELETS: The Cool Maker KumiFantasy Fashion Pack includes everything you need to create up to 12 friendship bracelets using the KumiKreator bracelet maker (sold separately)! KumiFantasy features 96 ready-to-use string spools in 5 fantasy-inspired colors, a bracelet design booklet, stylish clasps to customize and more!

96 PREMIUM SPOOLS: The KumiFantasy Fashion Pack’s 96 pre-loaded spools of string easily pop into the KumiKreator (sold separately) and make every bracelet look beautiful! Choose to create 8 or 12-strand bracelets from the design booklet for different bracelet looks. Stack, wrap and share your KumiFantasy bracelets with your BFF’s and mix and match with your outfits!

The Cool Maker KumiFantasy Fashion Pack is a jewelry making kit for Cool Makers aged 8 and up. Put the OMG in DIY and spin to create beautiful friendship bracelets with the KumiKreator and the KumiFantasy Fashion Pack! Cool Maker gives aspiring designers all the tools needed to make amazing creations they’ll be proud to share.
Includes: 96 Spools, 12 Clasps, 24 End Caps, 30 Clasp Stickers, 1 Design Booklet
description: Spin to create beautiful friendship bracelets with the Cool Maker KumiKreator bracelet maker and the KumiFantasy Fashion Pack! Drawing inspiration from the art of Japanese Kumi bracelets (Kumihimo in Japanese means “gathered threads”), the KumiKreator and the KumiFantasy Fashion Pack make it easy to create stylish and intricate Kumi friendship bracelets. This DIY kit features 96 ready-to-use spools of string in 5 fantasy-inspired colors to be used with the breakthrough KumiKreator (sold separately). The KumiFantasy Fashion Pack makes up to 12 unique and colorful bracelets! Select one of the stylish bracelet patterns from the design booklet, or create your own pattern! Next, count out the string spools following your bracelet design, load the spools into the KumiKreator and spin to create! As you turn the handle, the spools dance around the machine, magically weaving your bracelet together in minutes! When your bracelet is finished braiding, remove it from the machine and customize with a stylish clasp – no knots are needed! Stack, wrap and share your bracelets with your BFF’s and mix and match to accessorize every outfit! Braid beautiful friendship bracelets before your eyes with the KumiFantasy Fashion Pack and the KumiKreator!

title: Happy Atoms 2D: Interactive Chemistry Puzzles | Intro to Atoms, Molecules, Bonding | Create Thousands of Molecules with Card-Based, Jigsaw Puzzle Atoms & Free Educational App for iOS, Android
features: Build, scan, and identify molecules: the simplest way to learn about atoms, bonding, and chemistry.

In this 2D version of the Happy Atoms 3D physical and digital molecular modeling system, three-dimensional plastic atom models are replaced with flat, cardboard puzzle pieces representing 16 different elements: 14 Hydrogen atoms, 1 Helium atom, 2 Lithium atoms, 2 Beryllium atoms, 6 Carbon atoms, 3 Nitrogen atoms, 6 Oxygen atoms, 2 Fluorine atoms, 1 Neon atom, 2 Sodium atoms, 2 Magnesium atoms, 2 Silicon atoms, 2 Phosphorus atoms, 2 Sulfur atoms, 2 Chlorine atoms, and 1 Argon atom.
Includes the state-of-the-art Happy Atoms app (free download) with image recognition software and a small printed manual.
Bonus: Comes with a sample 3D Happy Atoms water molecule — H2O!
The app is available for Android and iOS devices.
description: Making sense of the world of atoms and molecules is now as easy as piecing together a jigsaw puzzle! Now you can use Happy Atoms, the revolutionary chemistry teaching tool, in a low-cost, two-dimensional jigsaw-puzzle-style edition. In this version, the three-dimensional plastic atoms have been replaced with flat, cardboard puzzle pieces. Just like in the original versions, you can build more than 17,000 molecules by combining the atoms of 16 elements and scanning them with the app to identify the molecules and learn about them. This kit comes with the same full-featured version of the Happy Atoms app that comes with the original versions of Happy Atoms. Bonus: Includes a sample 3D Happy Atoms water molecule — H2O! Using the Happy Atoms app and the camera on your tablet or smartphone running iOS or Android, you can scan the molecules you piece together. The app then uses state-of-the-art image recognition technology to identify the molecules. After a molecule is discovered, the app presents information about it, including its composition, usage, properties, hazards, formula, and structure. The app can recognize more than 17,000 molecules. It presents in-depth information about 160 molecules and general information about the rest. This app is a fun and interactive chemistry curriculum. It takes you on guided quests to discover new molecules and learn about them. You can track your progress with the app, collecting sets of molecules that you have built and explored.

review_samples.title: Homeschool perfection
review_samples.text: I had seen the small and large molecule set I really wanted it but honestly couldn't afford it and wasn't terribly sure if we liked it. When I saw this 2-d version all I could think was will it work with the app.... I'll admit you need good lighting and a white backdrop not included BUT nothing a white piece of paper can fix. My 10 year old daughter was learning about covalent bonds and making carbon dioxide and methane and learning the properties. Great buy and value ... works just like the big set ... However if the developer is listening I think you should update the app I was a smidge confused which I should pick... which made me hesitant to buy the product. As I wasnt sure if the 2d version worked with the app or was supposed to be used along side the large set.

review_samples.text: My latest order of ‘World Stamps For Less Worldwide 6 Sets from 43 Countries’ arrived a little less than a month early. The packet was due to arrive October 6. It showed up September 9. There were some stamps from Brasil in this pack, also, but this time they were of fish,instead of flowers. There were also stamps from the Comoros, Cook Islands Cyprus, Hellas(Greece), the Isle of Man, Malta, Niuafo’ou, (an island , belonging to Tonga), Papua New Guinea, and Samoa. They were beautiful stamps of beautiful colors with butterflies and statues on them. Another stamp I enjoyed was one from the ‘Principat D’Andorra, (French Andorra). It was a stamp of the French flag. I am very pleased with my latest order. My expectations were met, also.
