review_samples.title: Good Quality, but Poor Product Design Decisions
review_samples.text: I really wanted to like this puzzle, but after spending 3 hours assembling it, I am frustrated and disappointed by what could have been a really terrific product, but instead it is a a very poor product overall. The Good: - It comes in a very attractive little cardboard storage box - The plywood used is good quality and has a good feel in your hands - The plywood is sufficiently strong that it would be difficult to break any of the tabs without a tool or purposefully trying to snap them off - It is laser cut so all of the edges of the pieces are clean and smooth - It's a cat puzzle--who doesn't like a cat puzzle? - The image/picture looks and feels like it very securely attached to the wooden pieces, so I believe the image will not rub or peel off over time - The patterns/textures and colors used in the image are pleasing pastels and reminiscent of fine fabric patterns - The border pieces all have a narrow tan band outlining the entire puzzle. It makes it fairly easy to separate out the border pieces and get started on the puzzle - There are quite a few cool cat-silhouette shaped pieces scattered around the interior of the puzzle--what a cool idea! The Bad - The cute box does not have a latch or simple button to hold it closed and keep the pieces from spilling out or getting lost - The pieces are way, way too small, and the little tabs and slots can be difficult to put together for young hands or old hands. A typical piece is 5/8" x 3/8"--measuring from the outside edge of a tab to the outside edge of a tab on the opposite side of the piece, or 1/2" x 1/4" without tabs--the tabs are 1/16" to 1/8" long. - While laser cut, the laser still has a width, and that width is *relatively* large based on the size of the pieces. What this means is that the pieces fit together *very* loosely with a lot of slop. Since the borders of the puzzle aren't straight, this makes it difficult to properly form the shape of the border. - The slop (or 'play') between pieces also means that the connected pieces come apart under the gentlest of nudges. This is the frustration, where you found and fit some pieces together, then your palm brushes over them while you grab another piece and the pieces come apart! So, you are constantly putting back together and having to push the connected pieces back to their proper position. - The slop also makes it difficult to fit the next piece in. For example, when you've filled in an area except for one or two pieces that belong in the middle of the area, when you then try to fit one of the middle pieces in with, say, pieces on 3 sides of the new piece, the tabs and slots won't line up and you have to gently adjust the other puzzle pieces trying to get everything to line up. Finally, you do it, and the piece slips in where it belongs. But, lo! You've moved the other puzzle pieces enough that they've now disconnected from other puzzle pieces! More work that you've done has been undone, and has to be redone! - The box says this puzzle is good for ages 6 and up. I have known a lot of 6 year olds over the years, and not one of them could do this puzzle, even with help from an adult. A ten year old would have trouble maintaining their patience for this puzzle and have a lot of trouble trying to manipulate these tiny pieces, tabs, and slots. I think this is more appropriate for 14+ due to the piece size, the colors and patterns on the image, and the micro-size of tabs and slots. - I also would not recommend this puzzle for elderly (eyesight , dexterity, patience, and pastel color issues), certainly not a dementia or cognitively impaired adult - The picture of the completed puzzle is miniature, perhaps 1/4 of the size of the completed puzzle. It is very difficult to discern the fine patterns of the puzzle pieces and determine from the picture where the piece might go. - It shouldn't take 4 hours for two people to put this puzzle together, but that was our result due to the puzzle constantly coming apart (and we were trying to be careful!!) and the difficulty matching patterns on pieces to the picture. Note that we got the medium size. There is a large size, which is about 20% larger, but also has 300 pieces (vs. 200 pieces for the medium). So, each piece is about the same size between the two puzzles sizes. So I believe that the slop and disconnection problems we experienced with the medium puzzle still is a problem with the large puzzle due to the way it is made. My Recommendations to the Manufacturer 1. Your wood choice and the method that you attach the image to the wood stock is great, don't cut corners or change it. This could be a real high-quality, great product with a few changes to your design choices. 2. Scale the puzzle up by 1.6 - 2 times. This will make everything larger: the pieces easier to work with, the designs easier to see, and the relative size of the kerf will diminish meaning the pieces will fit together better and more securely (less relative slop and I bet the pieces won't slide out once they've been connected). 3. Keep the piece count at 200--if you increase the piece count because the area of the puzzle was increased, then you'll be back at the same problems as this puzzle has: kerf is too big relative to the piece size, leading to sloppy, loose fitting pieces that come apart too easily. 3. Scale the guide picture up by 2 times. Sure, the picture will have to be folded to fit in the box, but at least the picture will be easily visible and usable. 4. Attach a small plastic button to the lid on the box so that the box will snap shut and keep the pieces secure. Or use some other simple latching mechanism that won't break or tear in a short period of time. This is so close to being a great, long lasting puzzle. Scale up the puzzle, keep the piece count the same, keep the puzzle shapes exactly the same proportion (so the tabs and slots also get proportionally larger), and this will be a winner! As the puzzle is manufactured now, the puzzle is too frustrating to be fun.

review_samples.title: frustrating to work
review_samples.text: This puzzle comes beautifully packaged and gift boxed. However... it's very frustrating to work. The pieces are thick, but tiny (like the size of my thumbnail tiny), and the only picture of the finished piece is a 4x6 paper inside the box. My 48 year-old eyes go blurry after a little while working this puzzle. The details, such as various dotted patterns in different parts of the owl's body, are hard to see on such tiny pieces. I do enjoy finding the random animal shaped pieces such as a cat, a hummingbird, etc. But most frustrating of all, the pieces don't stay together while you're trying to attach another one-- they wiggle apart! So you wind up holding a group of attached pieces with one hand laying flat over top of them, while trying to fit together a new piece with the other hand. All in all, as much as I wanted to love this puzzle, it's just more frustrating than enjoyable for me.

review_samples.title: An awesome sequel
review_samples.text: Rather than being Santorini plus a little more, this new iteration of the game is more like a whole new game with just a little of Santorini left in it. Okay, maybe a little more than a little bit, but there's definitely a lot more to this game, and it is its own beast. Due to its various roles you can mix and match (only one of which, the Engineer, is required each game) almost every game you play can feel different for a very, very long time. If that's what you want ... in these types of games it can also be fun to repeatedly play a particular combo again and again to discover everything that set has to offer. It might be second only to Santorini itself in this respect. I feel there is a little too much going on to give this game as a gift to your average non-gamer family ... especially if a gamer isn't there to get them through the rules. I feel original Santorini is better in that respect. But for families who already play that level of game, Santorini New York would be a great next step.

review_samples.title: A lovely game, possibly better than the original
review_samples.text: I'm writing this review as someone who has played and enjoyed the original version of Santorini. First off, this game is not an expansion for Santorini and it's not a repackaging shell of the exact same game. I love that this was NOT a repackaging of the exact same game with a New York shell. The game plays differently. The basic mechanism of move then build and different character powers are there, but your power changes each turn you play and you have a hand of cards to choose from. There is strategy in which card you pick because it determines your power for that turn, but also the order you play in. The skyscrapers and Statue of Liberty are a nice twist to the game as well. I think it helped to have played the original version and really understand the basic mechanism (move then build) and movement rules, but I imagine people who are new to the game wouldn't have problems and would also enjoy the game on its own. You don't have to have played the original to have fun with this game. The game plays well with 2 and 3 players. We haven't tried more, but it is nice that 4 and 5 players have their own player tokens. In the original game if there's 4 + players you have to play on teams. I love the design and art of the game with its beautiful art deco cards and metallic foils on the box and cards. I also like the character design and movements like the pushy cop or the subway worker who can get out of obstacles by going "under" the buildings. This game is well worth the money! And a great value for the price point ($15). Tbh I think I might like Santorini: New York better than the original Santorini game.

review_samples.text: The wood on the back and front of the box is chipped. There's gunk where the dice would go; they didn't finish sanding the wood down and I fear the raised texture might chip some of my glass and gemstone dice. The velvet was poorly put in and bubbled up. Why doesn't it get a one star review? Because the etching on the wood, the picture of the wizard, looks great. When I smoothed out the velvet it rolled well. The magnets are strong, and it still looks good on a desk. I would have put it at three stars, but there's no excuse to send a damaged product out for sale.

review_samples.title: Doesn’t fit dice well
review_samples.text: The outside of the case is nice, has a smooth faux-leather feel. Good size to hold 6 sets of dice, and I liked how flat and portable it was. The problem is that the holes to hold the dice are cut outs shaped like the dice themselves but they are very poorly cut and don’t fit half of the shapes. review_samples.title: Fun but not her faves
review_samples.text: We got our daughter these and.a gear set for Christmas. She likes the gears better. These are something she’s only picked up a few times, but she does have fun with them when she does play with them. I’d advise getting the bigger set. review_samples.title: These bricks are great and colorful
review_samples.text: There are a bunch of smaller parts so I wouldn't recommend for anyone under 3 unsupervised. They are great, with a big variety of parts. I like that they have some with wheels so you can make cars. They are pretty easy to clean and keep clean. Would recommend.

review_samples.title: Creative shapes for creative play
review_samples.text: Great set of blocks for open ended play. These have the same concept as Lego blocks but instead of the typical nubs you place blocks on, these pieces have little "teeth" that secures the blocks together. It allows for more flexibility in how the blocks are positioned and placed with each other. The set does come with instructions to help get some ideas off the ground but its also fantastic to start playing blindly and see where your imagination takes you. Shapes are colorful, varied, and pretty well made. They can also interlock with other types of these "bristle" blocks as well, making fun even more endless. Very fun for both children and adults!

review_samples.title: Good source of entertainment
review_samples.text: These building bricks are sure very entertaining. We had another set like this in the past, we enjoyed it so much that we decided to add this one to our collection too. What I love about this set is it has more shapes than our old ones and also has the ones with wheels that my son surely appreciates. Theses bricks keep our kids busy for a good amount of time which gives me some kid free time to do my stuff done!

review_samples.title: Just meh
review_samples.text: Thought this would be a good valentines gift to do, but alas no. It has a 14 day journal to work on hygge and some finger knitting aspect to it (which needs better instructions—video is too fast and have to keep pausing and rewinding, then the instructions on the paper are incomplete does not show how to tie it off only does this in words.) make a better video or better paper instructions. The only plus we had from that activity was that we laughed so hard at each others messes we made. Then there is some activity cards that you fill out (which doesn’t take too long) and one tiny piece of fairy lights. One sticker and one magnet. Not even fancy pens but 2 mini score pencils! The last thing was the tiny cards that had a bunch of questions on them. I don’t know, but if I am going to pay $$$ for a date night box I expect more than just one fillable card and a bunch of question cards as the main pieces! I mean at least put in some fancy pens! Those pencils were just sad!! The fairy lights were just over a foot long, what can you fancy up with that?! This box is horrible and for the price I could have bought a different set of question cards that would have done the same thing and a nicer set of lights and cost half as much! I have bought these boxes before and this one is by far the worst, think I am done with these, either this was one of the first ones out or their products have gone downhill.

review_samples.title: Lots of laughs and tons of fun!
review_samples.text: We had a fantastic time. Everything was so cute and on theme with the music playlist, the automated assistant, the props, and the activities. review_samples.title: Dino Bank
review_samples.text: This plastic dinosaur bank is very cute and true to picture. The paint quality is not quite as neat as I'd like it to be, but for a baby's first bank it will do just fine.

review_samples.title: Adorable piggy bank
review_samples.text: My 5yr old eagle eye'd this one and had to have it - and figured it was time to replace his ceramic elephant if anything, just for safety sake. Plus he's a huge dino fan - so this was an easy win! I did measure this to answer a FAQ on here, but it's about 8" tall by 8" length to the tail and 5.5" wide, measuring the feet, to give some idea of the size of the bank. Cute, unbreakable, holds money with a secure lid - all you could ask for from a kid's piggy bank!

review_samples.title: Super cute bank and a great gift for a little one
review_samples.text: [[VIDEOID:da9a20fee81098d0eb461fdeb0fc2bf3]] This is a very nice bank to give any little one that enjoys dinosaurs. The item came promptly, and it was packaged very nicely. The box arrived, and was torn open and repaired with tape but that’s not on the seller that’s on Amazon. The item itself was in good condition inside the box. The little dinosaur measures a bow 7 inches tall and is made from very heavy duty plastic which means it’ll be shatterproof and can resist the little one throwing it on the floor to play with it. My child loved it when he first saw it, and actually thought it was a toy. Despite being a bank, he actually plays with it like it’s a doll with his other toys. The dinosaur is very cute but actually is a bit darker green than the advertisement photo show. I didn’t mind this because I like the dark green color a bit more but if you had your heart set on the light green, you see in the photos just be warned. It’s easy to open and since it’s so big has plenty of room for coins and cash for the little ones. This is a really nice item and would make a great gift. Thumbs up

review_samples.title: An fun-filled instant camera for the kids
review_samples.text: This instant camera for kids is well-made and promises lots of fun because it does so many things like take pictures (including a selfie), record videos, play games, and play an MP3. It is perfect for small hands to hold, but it also comes with a lanyard that has a detachable button. This camera is sturdy and can take some roughness like being dropped or splashed. It is rechargeable and the screen displays the remaining battery power. The charging port and SD card slot are safely covered. It can print pictures right after they are taken, but that can also be turned off. All the photos and videos taken are stored in the 32GB SD card included. They can all be viewed by going to the “Playback Mode” which is one of the tabs among the 6 folders. Print quality is decent. The images are printed in different shades of gray and reflect a decent reproduction of what was taken. Pictures can have a fun photo frame or have messages. Each photo always prints on a 4" x 2.25" paper that the kids can color using the markers included. Three rolls of regular thermal paper are part of the package.

review_samples.title: The Walking Dead Walk With Two Right Hands and Two Left Feet.
review_samples.text: So I really liked this product until I realized that the costume came with two right hand gloves. My son has both a right and a left hand. I tried to send back for a replacement but UPS stated that it is “against our policy to ship small children across the country,” and “there is nothing wrong with how the boy’s hands are oriented.” Sigh.

review_samples.title: Okay for a quick costume
review_samples.text: This year i didnt feel like going all out for a costume so i took my search to amazon. My 6 year old chose this one. We recieved it quick which was awesome. The material was super stretchy and panty hose like... not the greatest. The frayed pieces ripped off ina. Few spots and there was a hole in it within 2 hours of putting it on. Ok for a last minute quick costume but not worth any more than $20.

review_samples.title: Fingers crossed you get the right size.
review_samples.text: Sizes are way off!! Luckily my 8 year old isn’t too big of a kid or he wouldn’t be able to get this on at all. I ordered the medium which would be an 8-10 we got a 3T. (3T wasn’t even an option to order) With some extra clothes underneath we made it work. I don’t have time to send back and get the right size. It is a cool costume with the axe and mask. The outfit is see through but stretchy so typical for costumes.

review_samples.title: Really great costume!
review_samples.text: This costume is so great. Quality is pretty good, better than you’d expect from a big Halloween store. Ordered the size 3t for my petite 4 year old, and it fits her perfectly, other than the gloves. The gloves are my only complain. They fit me, a 31 year old. They are in no way child gloves. My daughter is disappointed because they obviously won’t stay on her hands. Other than that, this is an awesome costume.

review_samples.title: Would buy again
review_samples.text: Boys loved it.
